question: Who issued the silver rupee, which remained a standard coin for centuries after the ruler?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sher Shah Suri**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• Sher Shah Suri was the founder of the Sur Empire in North India, ruling from 1540 to 1545.

• He issued the silver rupee coin, also known as the "Rupiya", which weighed 178 grains (11.53 grams).

• The silver rupee introduced by Sher Shah Suri became the standard currency of medieval India and continued to be used during the Mughal period and the British Raj.

• The introduction of this standardized currency helped in facilitating trade and commerce across his empire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Sher Shah Suri (1486-1545)**

• Born as Farid Khan, he was the founder of the Sur Empire in North India.

• He is known for his administrative and military prowess, establishing a well-organized system of governance.

• He introduced several reforms including the introduction of the "Rupiya", improved road infrastructure, and a postal system.

• His reign, though short, had a lasting impact on the subsequent Mughal administration.

• **Rupiya**

• The "Rupiya" was the standardized silver coin introduced by Sher Shah Suri, which weighed 178 grains (approximately 11.53 grams).

• This coin became the precursor to the modern rupee and was widely accepted across the Indian subcontinent.

• The introduction of the "Rupiya" facilitated trade and commerce by providing a reliable and standardized medium of exchange.

• It continued to be the standard currency during the Mughal period and later under British rule.

• **Standardization of Currency**

• Standardization of currency refers to the introduction of a uniform system of coins or notes that are accepted as a medium of exchange within a particular region or country.

• This helps in reducing confusion and fraud, facilitating smoother trade and commerce.

• Sher Shah Suri's introduction of the silver "Rupiya" is an early example of currency standardization in India.

• Standardized currency systems are crucial for the economic stability and growth of a nation.

• **Impact on Trade and Commerce**

• The introduction of a standardized currency like the "Rupiya" played a significant role in boosting trade and commerce.

• Merchants and traders had a reliable medium of exchange which was widely accepted.

• This facilitated long-distance trade and contributed to the economic prosperity of the empire.

• The benefits of a standardized currency system were evident in the economic policies of subsequent rulers.
